summary: [¶] (m) Thereafter, UPPCL made payment of the Change in Law claim on 24.5.2021. Subsequently, the Petitioner _vide_ its letters dated 4.6.2021 and 11.10.2021 requested TPTCL to arrange for payment of LPS from UPPCL in terms of Clause 18.11(g) of the RfP for the delay in payment of the CIL Claim. Accordingly, TPTCL _vide_ its letters dated 7.6.2021, 13.10.2021, and 8.12.2021 requested UPPCL to arrange for the release of LPS in terms of Clause 18.11(g) of the RfP due to the delay in releasing the Change in Law claim. However, UPPCL did not respond to the aforesaid letters. In view of the same, UPPCL sought time to file an affidavit, stating that the necessary documents were submitted by the Petitioner only in April 2021, and payment was made thereafter in May 2021. UPPCL also requested a further oral hearing, whereas TPTCL confirmed that it had already filed its affidavit in compliance with earlier directions. [para 21] 21. We have considered the submissions of both parties. We note that the gravamen of the Petitioner emanates from the delay in honouring the invoices by the Respondent UPPCL in light of the order passed in Petition No. 158/MP/2017. According to the Respondent, UPPCL carrying cost, and the LPS claimed by the Petitioner in the present Petition are not maintainable in view of provisions of Order II Rule 2 of the CPC and also in light of constructive _res-judicata_ under Section 11 of the CPC. The Respondent UPPCL has submitted that since the Petitioner omitted to claim LPS in the main Petition, the Petitioner cannot be allowed to file a subsequent Petition to claim the relief so omitted. On the other hand, the Petitioner has submitted that the issue raised is squarely covered by the Commission’s decision dated 9.8.2023 in Petition No. 173/MP/2022, wherein a similar objection was raised and rejected by the Commission. It has also been submitted by the Petitioner that since the entitlement of LPS arose upon delay in payment made by Respondent UPPCL, the same claim could not have been raised in the original Change in Law Petition No. 158/MP/2017. [para 27] 27. In the present case, the claim of the Petitioner for the LPS on the Change in Law compensation is premised on an entirely different and distinct cause of action than its claim for the Change in Law compensation. The former is premised on the Respondent UPPCL having failed to honour the invoices raised towards the Change in Law compensation and cannot said to be a ground of attack/claim that is essentially connected with or incidental to the Change in Law determination as involved in earlier Petition No. 158/MP/2017 filed by the Petitioner. Also, the Commission in its order dated 9.8.2023 in Petition No. 173/MP/2022 has observed that the “right to sue” in relation to LPS claims can begin to run only when there is a default in making the payment of LPS, which can only be subsequent to the crystallization of the LPS liability, i.e. date on which the payment towards the invoices has been made. In view of the same, in the present case, the Petitioner could not have claimed the same in the original Petition No. 158/MP/2017, as the Petitioner’s right to claim LPS crystallized only upon the payment of the principal amount by Respondent UPPCL, i.e., on 24.5.2021.
